title: Architecture scan
description: Three structural patterns a graph cannot settle: a service grown past one responsibility, a concept implemented twice, and a concept spelled out repeatedly rather than named. The taxonomy this comes from carried five more — import cycle, layer violation, domain file holding a transport or storage construct, hidden shared state, and undeclared debt — each decided by walking a graph or comparing two lists, which foundation/0004 R6 puts in a script. `thresholds_used` exists because every numeric bound the source agent shipped was uncalibrated: foundation/0006 R21 admits only a threshold calibrated from executed runs, so a value reaches this artifact from the caller or from observation, and R22 makes it say which. `framework` is not an admissible source for one.

scan_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

scanned.description: Every path the scan covered. An empty findings array means nothing without it.

thresholds_used.description: Every numeric value the scan applied. Empty means none was applied and the findings rest on judgement alone, which is the default: this capability ships no threshold.

source.description: `caller` supplied for this run; `observed` counted from the scanned set. There is deliberately no `framework` value — a shipped threshold would need calibration recorded with the evidence that produced it, and none exists.

findings.description: One entry per match, sorted by the first site's path. Empty is a real result.

pattern.description: Closed at three. The five removed are a script's, and reporting both kinds here would make the script's findings look like opinions.

sites.description: Every site, not a representative one: the cost of the finding is proportional to how many places must change together.

evidence.description: What was observed, quoted or counted, never inferred from naming.

cost.description: What goes wrong later if it stays, as a consequence rather than a verdict. Naming a violated principle is not a cost.
